entities.summary: Henri Calloc'h de Kérillis was a French aviator, reporter, writer and politician. A hero of World War I, he traveled widely in the 1920s, and wrote several books about his adventures. He became a journalist, then entered politics as an independent Republican. He was right-wing, conservative and profoundly nationalist. He was hostile to the parties that favored appeasement of Germany in the lead-up to World War II, and went into exile rather than be arrested after the armistice of July 1940. At first a strong supporter of Charles de Gaulle and his Free French, he later fell out with de Gaulle too.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a hero of World War I and a vocal critic of appeasement, Henri de Kérillis's nationalist views influenced French politics in the interwar period. His exile after the armistice of July 1940 marked a significant turning point in his relationship with Charles de Gaulle.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a hero of World War I and a vocal critic of appeasement, Henri de Kérillis's nationalist views influenced French politics in the lead-up to World War II. His exile after the armistice had significant regional implications for France's post-war trajectory.
